confirm.title: DoLu backend
confirm.description:
A DoLu backend announced itself as **{name}** at {host}, version {version}.

Everything on this screen comes from that network announcement, and anyone on the network can write one of those. Nothing has been verified yet.

To pair, open the DoLu admin panel, go to **Home Assistant → Pairing**, and generate a code. It is shown once and lasts ten minutes.

code.title: Pairing code
code.description:
Type the code generated in the DoLu admin panel of {name} ({host}).

The code is never sent: it is used to check that the backend on the other end knows it too. If it does not, this flow stops without sending anything.

verify.title: Check the fingerprint
verify.description:
**{name}** at {host}, version {version}, proved it knows the pairing code.

Fingerprint of the certificate that actually served this connection:

**{fingerprint}**

Compare it against the one shown in the DoLu admin panel. They must match character for character. If they do not, cancel: something on the network is impersonating your backend.

On confirming, Home Assistant will create an admin user called **DoLu**, local-network only and with no password to log in with, and hand the backend a token for it. You can revoke it at any time by deleting that user under Settings → People.

user.title: Add a DoLu backend
user.description: Use this when the backend is not discovered on its own, which is what happens when Home Assistant and the backend are on different networks.

verify_unused.title: Check the fingerprint
verify_unused.description:
**{name}** at {host}, version {version}, proved it knows the pairing code, and the fingerprint of the certificate that served this connection is:

**{fingerprint}**

Compare it against the DoLu admin panel before going on.

⚠️ **This backend will not use what it is given.** It has `HA_BASE_URL` and `HA_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN` in its `.env` file, and those take precedence over paired credentials: they will be stored, but it will keep talking to the Home Assistant from the `.env`. This is on purpose, so that a pairing cannot disconnect a backend that was set up by hand.

If you continue, the **DoLu** user and its token will still be created. To make them count, remove those two lines from the backend's `.env` and restart it.

error.invalid_code: That code is not the one this backend is waiting for — or whatever answered is not your backend. Nothing was sent. Check the code shown in the DoLu panel, or generate a new one. This does not use up any of the code's five attempts.
error.code_expired: The backend has no active code: the last one expired. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and type it here.
error.code_used: The backend has no active code: the last one was already used, and codes work once. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and type it here.
error.code_locked: The backend has no active code: the last one was blocked after five failed attempts. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and type it here.
error.no_active_code: The backend has no active pairing code. Generate one in the DoLu admin panel, under Home Assistant → Pairing, and type it here.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the backend over HTTPS. Check that it is running and that the address and port are right.
error.too_many_requests: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute and try again.
error.unexpected_response: The backend answered something unexpected. Check that its version matches this integration.

abort.already_configured: This DoLu backend is already set up.
abort.incomplete_discovery: The announcement did not carry the backend identity. Check that the backend is running a version that announces itself (0.3.30 or newer).
abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one DoLu backend can be set up: there is one per home.
abort.ignored_entry: This DoLu backend is set as ignored in Home Assistant. Stop ignoring it (Settings → Devices & services → ⋮ → Show ignored integrations) before adding it by hand.
abort.fingerprint_mismatch: The certificate served does not match the announced fingerprint. Someone on the network is impersonating your DoLu backend, so nothing was sent. Check the backend and the network before trying again.
abort.identity_mismatch: The backend identified itself as a different installation than the one announced. Nothing was sent.
abort.invalid_proof: The backend rejected this Home Assistant's proof. Generate a new code and start again.
abort.session_lost: The pairing conversation expired. Generate a new code in the DoLu admin panel and start again.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach the backend over HTTPS.
abort.code_expired: Pairing did not finish: the code expired first. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and start again.
abort.code_used: Pairing did not finish: the code was spent along the way. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and start again.
abort.code_locked: Pairing did not finish: the code was blocked after five failed attempts. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and start again.
abort.no_active_code: Pairing did not finish: the backend no longer has an active code. Generate a new one in the DoLu admin panel and start again.
abort.too_many_requests: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute and start again.
abort.onboarding_incomplete: Finish Home Assistant's initial setup first. Pairing now would leave the user DoLu creates as the owner of this installation, and that is not easy to undo.
abort.no_ha_url: Home Assistant has no address to give the backend. Set one under Settings → System → Network (local address) and try again.
abort.user_failed: The DoLu user could not be created in Home Assistant. Check the log for why; nothing was delivered to the backend.
abort.token_failed: The DoLu token could not be created. Nothing was delivered to the backend, and anything created along the way was undone.
abort.token_refused: Home Assistant refused to create the DoLu token. That usually means an earlier one is still there and could not be removed: delete the DoLu user under Settings → People and pair again.
